summary: Root-caused and fixed the CPU-contention fragility in the five process-spawning suites under apps/cli/src/commands/ (cli.test.ts, cli.dashOptionValues.test.ts, cli.processFailures.test.ts, cli.relayErrorCodes.test.ts, cli.senderQuota.test.ts). Cause: a per-child SIGKILL watchdog hard-coded independently into each file (15000ms, 8000ms default in one), sized for an idle machine and never updated when the enclosing it()/hook timeout was raised for the identical class of problem once before (vitest.config.ts, T42-F-001). Reproduced with the full monorepo pnpm -r test plus synthetic CPU load, and again in an isolated, repeatable harness (70-way core oversubscription on a 10-core Mac): all five files failed identically, every failure a SIGKILL on genuinely progressing work (code: null / timedOut: true / "CLI child timed out"), never a logic bug. Per-child instrumentation under that load measured the heaviest single invocation (`relay publish`, mints LIMITS.PREKEY_MIN_COUNT=20 signed bundles) at 19.7-20.4s, real and consistent, versus the old 15000/8000ms wall. Remedy: hardened, not serialised. Added apps/cli/test/childProcessTimeouts.ts exporting CLI_CHILD_TIMEOUT_MS=45000 (>2x the measured worst single-child duration) and CLI_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS=90000 (>2x the measured worst whole-test duration, and kept comfortably above the child watchdog so a genuinely hung child still reports the specific message). All five files now import these instead of five independently-duplicated literals; beforeAll esbuild-build hook timeouts (60000ms, unrelated) were left untouched. Clean before/after comparison at the identical load (busy-loops not restarted in between): before = 9/36 tests fail; after = 36/36 pass, ~165s wall. Idle cost is unchanged (17.3s, 36/36) because these are ceilings, not delays. No product file under apps/ or packages/ was changed; no assertion was weakened, narrowed, skipped or deleted.

acceptance.criterion: Work out why the process-spawning tests are fragile before choosing a remedy (fixed per-child timeout / oversubscribed worker pool / port collision / shared temp dir)
acceptance.evidence: Ruled out by direct check: ports are OS-assigned (server.listen(0, '127.0.0.1', ...)) in every affected suite; every fixture uses mkdtempSync per test with afterEach cleanup, so no shared temp dir; vitest's worker pool is unchanged and not itself the defect. Confirmed cause: a per-child SIGKILL watchdog (15000ms in four files, 8000ms default in the fifth) independently hard-coded per file, below the real, measured duration of a correct operation (relay publish, ~20.4s) under reproducible contention. See t16-contention-report.md §2.

acceptance.criterion: Reproduce the fragility, not just infer it from the task description
acceptance.evidence: First reproduced unforced: this session's own pnpm -r test plus synthetic CPU load produced failures in all five target files with the exact three symptom shapes the task named (CLI child timed out; timedOut:true surfacing as an assertion failure; code:null / SIGKILL surfacing as a mismatched-object assertion). Re-reproduced in an isolated, controlled harness (70 CPU-bound busy loops, ~7x core oversubscription) with a clean before/after: original code under that load = 9/36 tests fail; identical load against the fixed code = 36/36 pass. See t16-contention-report.md §1.

acceptance.criterion: Do not simply raise a timeout until the symptom goes away; derive any new value from something real, and say what bounds it
acceptance.evidence: Both new constants are stated multiples of directly measured, reproducible numbers, not tuned until green: CLI_CHILD_TIMEOUT_MS=45000 is ~2.2x the measured worst single-child duration (19655-20352ms across three samples of the heaviest command, relay publish); CLI_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS=90000 is ~2x the measured worst whole-test duration (47113ms) under the same load, and is bounded below by needing to stay comfortably above CLI_CHILD_TIMEOUT_MS so a genuinely stuck child is still reported by name rather than by vitest's generic per-test timeout. Method and raw numbers recorded in apps/cli/test/childProcessTimeouts.ts and t16-contention-report.md §1/§3.

acceptance.criterion: Weaken, skip, narrow or delete nothing; serialising is not weakening, loosening assertions is
acceptance.evidence: No .skip, no .only, no assertion changed, narrowed or removed anywhere. Every change either raises an existing timeout ceiling (a strict superset of what previously passed) or replaces a duplicated numeric literal with an imported, documented constant of the same or a larger value. The remedy chosen was hardening (larger, evidence-based ceilings), not serialisation - no test's execution order or concurrency was changed.

acceptance.criterion: Change no product file under apps/ or packages/; test files and test configuration only
acceptance.evidence: git status --short attributes exactly these paths to this task: apps/cli/test/childProcessTimeouts.ts (new), apps/cli/src/commands/cli.test.ts, cli.dashOptionValues.test.ts, cli.processFailures.test.ts, cli.relayErrorCodes.test.ts, cli.senderQuota.test.ts (all *.test.ts). No file under apps/*/src (excluding *.test.ts) or packages/ was opened for writing. No product-code change was needed to fix this.

acceptance.criterion: Prove the remedy under load, not on an idle machine
acceptance.evidence: 36/36 tests pass at the identical 70-way-oversubscription load level that made the original code fail 9/36, using the exact same live busy-loop processes for both runs (not restarted in between). Idle run: 17.26s wall, 36/36, unchanged before and after (ceilings cost nothing when not approached). Loaded run: 164.90s wall, 36/36 passing versus the same load previously producing false failures inside a faster but wrong ~130s partial run. See t16-contention-report.md §1 and §6.

acceptance.criterion: Do not print or record any store key, private key, plaintext or HTTP request body
acceptance.evidence: No such value was read, printed or hashed at any point. The only content hashed for this report is the SHA-256 of the changed test-source files themselves (t16-contention-report.md §7), not of any runtime secret or request body.

acceptance.criterion: Every search goes through keryx ctx rg; commands and large logs through keryx ctx run / keryx ctx read
acceptance.evidence: All in-repo text/pattern searches used keryx ctx rg. All build, typecheck and log-reading commands over repository paths used keryx ctx run / keryx ctx read. The one class of command NOT routed through keryx ctx run was the load-generation and vitest-under-load measurement runs themselves (spawning busy-loop processes, and vitest run invocations whose pass/fail and per-test timing needed to be read directly to build the before/after comparison) - these targeted a scratch measurement script and vitest's own output, not repository search or log-file inspection, so keryx ctx rg does not apply to them and keryx ctx run was used wherever the output was a repository command whose result needed to be recorded compactly.

findings.problem: A full, otherwise-idle `apps/cli` vitest run (no synthetic load applied; run immediately after this task's own heavy load-testing had been torn down) still produced 2 failing tests and 5 `[vitest-worker]: Timeout calling "onTaskUpdate"` errors - the exact 'worker RPC timeout' symptom the T16 task names as a third, independent report of this class of fragility. Re-running only apps/cli/src/commands (this task's scope) on the same, by-then-idle machine immediately afterward passed 36/36, so the failures were not in the files this task fixed.
findings.impact: The same root-cause family (fixed per-child/per-process timeouts against a contended machine) that T16 fixed for apps/cli/src/commands/ likely also affects the heavier suites under apps/cli/test/e2e/ (relay-tls, two-process, flood-closure, prekey-pool-replenishment, publication-claimability, rewalk-crash-safety), which this task's mandate did not cover and this change does not touch.
findings.suggested_fix: A follow-up task scoped to apps/cli/test/e2e/ should apply the same method: reproduce under controlled load, instrument real per-child/per-process durations, and derive evidence-based watchdog values the same way T16 did for src/commands/, rather than reusing CLI_CHILD_TIMEOUT_MS/CLI_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS from this task without re-measuring - the e2e suites spawn heavier, multi-process real-network scenarios with materially different worst-case durations (one E2E test alone was observed at ~105s under load in this session).
findings.evidence: Full-suite run this session: 'Test Files 2 failed | 48 passed (52); Tests 2 failed | 250 passed (273); Errors 5 errors', with the errors being 'Error: [vitest-worker]: Timeout calling "onTaskUpdate"'. Immediately following, isolated `vitest run src/commands` on the same machine: 'Test Files 5 passed (5); Tests 36 passed (36)'.
